newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba sends managers back to accounting classroom.
newsitem.headline: Cuba sends managers back to accounting classroom.

text.p: Alarmed by undisciplined accounting in state-run firms, Cuban authorities plan to send managers back to the classroom for lessons on basic bookkeeping and finances.

The ruling Communist Party daily Granma reported on Friday that managers in a wide range of state sectors, including companies and local government, will this year undergo training courses that include a basic programme on accountancy.

Granma said managers who take the courses, organised by the Higher Education Ministry and Havana University, will be evaluated at the end. And those managers whose knowledge is considered sufficient for them to skip the training will have to take exams anyway.
As a result no one will get a job as a manager without a certificate showing basic business knowledge.

According to deputy president Carlos Lage, who has led meetings in recent months to examine efficiency in various state sectors, "there is no doubt a generalized weakness in the economy in internal control and accountancy", Granma noted.

Put another way, too much money is falling through the cracks in state-run enterprises. It is money the ailing Cuban economy can ill afford, especially if it is lost by firms involved in the hard currency sector.

Government subsidies for state firms have been steadily reduced in recent years, as Cuba seeks to emerge from crisis triggered by the collapse of its old economic partner, the former Soviet Union. Companies have been told to make themselves profitable and efficient.
